result:
I've saved the workbook to `extraction/stec.xlsx` with the four sheets in the required order. The ledger has 67 rows in one process, split into three rounds.

Every quotation was matched by script against my text copy of the filing, on the page it cites. A script also confirmed that sort dates never go backwards, all value lists are respected, every bid row is complete, and the flags match the Questions. Every bidder's participation reconciles, with only WDC still open at the end, as the winner.

**How the sale went.** sTec's board began a strategic review in late 2012, with an activist, Balch Hill, pressing in parallel, and set up a special committee on 02/13/2013. Companies A, B, C and D approached early. BofA Merrill Lynch was hired in late March and from 04/01/2013 had discussions with 18 prospective buyers. Six signed confidentiality agreements. Companies C, E and F wanted only selected assets, and G dropped out.

Three bidders made offers for the whole company in round 1: WDC ($6.60–7.10), D ($5.75) and H, a late entrant ($5.00–5.75). Only WDC and D were sent final-round letters with a draft merger agreement. WDC bid $9.15 with a markup of the agreement while D kept asking for more time, and the board chose WDC on 05/30. WDC pulled out the next day. D was invited to continue but dropped out on 06/05. WDC came back on 06/10 with a $6.60–7.10 range and was told to name one best price. It bid $6.85, which the board accepted without countering. The merger was signed 06/23/2013 and announced 06/24/2013.

**Questions and my recommendations**
- **Q1:** The filing doesn't say who most of the 18 parties were. I left the count of remaining contacted companies as "12–14" rather than a single number, because B and C may or may not be among the 18.
- **Q2:** E and F count as bidders for the whole company (their confidentiality agreements were for a sale of the company) and as withdrawing when they switched to wanting only assets. C was only ever interested in assets, so it stays outside the count.
- **Q3:** One process with three rounds, opening 03/26, 05/16 and 05/31. The third round is my inference: D was reopened after WDC withdrew. The alternatives are moving round 2's start to 05/10, or having no round 3.
- **Q4:** The 05/03 due date was extended because D's late 05/10 offer was accepted.
- **Q5:** H was kept in reserve rather than dropped, and I record its exit as "not selected at signing", because it would not raise its price.
- **Q6:** WDC's 06/10 and 06/14 offers count as formal because they refer back to its 05/28 terms. I rated their conditions "Unclear" rather than "Heavy", because the insider agreements are only stated as a condition in the signed agreement.
- **Q7:** For round 2, 05/28 was extended and 05/30 enforced. WDC's 05/30 confirmation of $9.15 is not a reaffirmed bid.
- **Q8:** WDC withdrew on 05/31 (the filing says "at that time") and re-entered on 06/10.

**Limitations**
- The filing names only a few of the 18 parties, so the size of the contacted group stays a range.
- The filing encodes its punctuation in an old Windows format. I converted it to curly apostrophes, quotes and dashes, so if the reviewer's matching script expects straight characters, those quotations will need normalizing.
- I built the file with a Python library and checked it by script; I haven't opened it in Excel to look at the layout.
